notes: Grab (taxi/moto) is cheap; red songthaew 30-60 THB; scooter 250/day (licence needed). The airport is 15 minutes from the city.

November to February is cool and dry (best; Yi Peng lantern festival and Loy Krathong in November); March to April brings burning smoke (air pollution is bad, bring a mask), and the Songkran water fight is in April.
TDAC digital arrival card; Turkish citizens get 60 days visa-free. Bring cash in THB; cards work in malls.
Khao soi 50-70, street food 40-60, restaurant 150-250; elephant park 2,500, cooking class 1,200-1,500; round up tips.
Cover shoulders and knees in temples; NO elephant riding, sanctuaries only. Visit Doi Suthep in the morning and the Sunday Walking Street in the evening.
Coffee culture is in Nimman; Akha Ama, Ristr8to, Graph.

stops.name: Wat Phra Singh
stops.tips: Golden Lanna-style temple with the Lion Buddha; come in the morning to see the monks.

stops.name: Wat Chedi Luang
stops.tips: Giant brick stupa from 1391 (partly ruined by an earthquake); join a monk chat in the afternoon.

stops.name: Khao Soi Khun Yai
stops.tips: Northern Thailand's coconut curry noodle soup (khao soi); closes at 14:00, Sri Phum.

stops.name: Three Kings Monument & Lanna Folklife Museum
stops.tips: The three founding kings and a museum of Lanna culture (air-conditioned).

stops.name: Tha Phae Gate
stops.tips: Old city gate with pigeons; on Sundays the Walking Street starts here.

backups.name: SP Chicken
backups.tips: Skewered grilled chicken (gai yang); next to Wat Phra Singh.

backups.name: Wat Chiang Man
backups.tips: The city's oldest temple (1296); elephant stupa, a stand-in for the museum.

stops.name: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
stops.tips: Mountain temple at 1,000 m; red songthaew 60 THB, 306-step naga staircase, golden stupa and city views, quiet in the morning.

stops.name: Wat Pha Lat
stops.tips: Hidden temple in the forest; 45-minute descent along the Monk's Trail, waterfall.

stops.name: Nimmanhaemin Road
stops.tips: Nimman: cafes, One Nimman, Think Park, boutiques.

stops.name: Tong Tem Toh Nimman
stops.tips: Northern Thai cooking; nam prik ong (pork and tomato chilli dip) and sai oua sausage, expect a queue.

stops.name: Maya Mall Rooftop Bar
stops.tips: Sunset and mountain views in Nimman; quick stop.

backups.name: Chiang Mai University Ang Kaew Lake
backups.tips: Campus lake with mountain views; a stand-in for Nimman.

stops.name: Elephant Nature Park
stops.tips: Sanctuary for rescued elephants; NO riding, feeding and a walk in the river, book online months ahead, vegetarian lunch included, hotel pickup 60 km.

stops.name: Mae Taeng River Viewpoint
stops.tips: Valley views on the way back; photo stop.

stops.name: Huen Phen
stops.tips: Restaurant in a 1970s Lanna house; khantoke platter, rooms full of antiques.

backups.name: Dash! Restaurant Old City
backups.tips: Thai food in a teak house; a stand-in for Huen Phen.

stops.name: Doi Inthanon Summit
stops.tips: Thailand's highest point at 2,565 m; 2 hours by tour or rental car, 10°C in the morning, Ang Ka moss forest trail.

stops.name: King & Queen Pagodas
stops.tips: Twin pagodas and gardens; sea of clouds.

stops.name: Wachirathan Waterfall
stops.tips: Thundering 80 m waterfall; rainbows.

stops.name: Pha Dok Siew Nature Trail
stops.tips: 2.5 km through forest and rice terraces with a Karen village guide; coffee in Mae Klang Luang village.

stops.name: Mae Klang Luang Karen Village
stops.tips: Lunch on a terrace; village coffee and fish.

backups.name: Royal Project Inthanon Restaurant
backups.tips: Royal Project agricultural station; trout and strawberries.

stops.name: Thai Farm Cooking School
stops.tips: Cooking class on an organic farm; market shopping, 5 dishes (khao soi, curry paste), hotel pickup.

stops.name: Warorot Market Kad Luang
stops.tips: Locals' market; dried fruit, sai oua, Lanna fabrics, Chinatown.

stops.name: Wat Ket Karam & Ping River
stops.tips: Temple and cafes across the river; Wat Ket neighbourhood.

stops.name: Woo Cafe Ping River
stops.tips: Gallery cafe; riverside.

stops.name: Night Bazaar Chiang Mai
stops.tips: Chang Khlan night market; open every night, bargain, Kalare food court.

backups.name: Basil Cookery School
backups.tips: Class in the Old City; a stand-in for the farm.

backups.name: Ploen Ruedee Night Market
backups.tips: Food courtyard with live music next to the night market.

stops.name: Bua Tong Sticky Waterfall
stops.tips: Climb the limestone 'sticky' waterfall (non-slip); 1 hour north of the city, free.

stops.name: Mae Kampong Village
stops.tips: Mountain village in the clouds; tea and coffee, wooden houses, Thai villagers.

stops.name: Mae Kampong Village Restaurant
stops.tips: Local miang (fermented tea leaves) and northern dishes.

stops.name: Mae Kampong Waterfall
stops.tips: Seven-tier waterfall in the village; walk.

stops.name: Flight of the Gibbon Zipline
stops.tips: Forest zipline (optional, expensive); or the San Kamphaeng hot springs.

backups.name: San Kamphaeng Hot Springs
backups.tips: Foot soak and boiled eggs at the hot springs; a stand-in for the zipline.

backups.name: Mae Kampong Coffee House
backups.tips: Village coffee and miang; a lighter stand-in for the restaurant.

days.theme: Sunday Walking Street and a gentle goodbye

stops.name: Wat Umong
stops.tips: Tunnel temple in the forest; monks' sayings hang in the trees.

stops.name: Baan Kang Wat Artists' Village
stops.tips: Wooden workshop village; ceramics, cafe, next to Wat Umong.

stops.name: Khao Soi Mae Sai
stops.tips: The locals' khao soi; Ratchaphuek.

stops.name: Chiang Mai Airport
stops.tips: 15 minutes from the city by Grab; goodbye.

backups.name: Sunday Walking Street Ratchadamnoen
backups.tips: If it's Sunday: a 1 km handicraft market with temple courtyard food; book a late flight.
